revisedPrompt:
Use case: identity-preserve. Create FOUR COMPLETE Chronos robot-and-held-hammer sprite drawings, as a clean transparent 2x2 animation sheet with equal 640x640 cells, fixed front camera, common boot baseline and identical body unit. References 1 and 2 lock the original robot and exact small dark finned helmet / single cyan visor. Reference 3 locks the original blue electric CYLINDRICAL T-HAMMER. Preserve these designs, black segmented shaft and both round black-rimmed END CAPS. Detailed sharp 16-bit metallic sprite style. His original head stays upright LOOKING STRAIGHT AT THE VIEWER in every pose. Whole actor and held weapon drawn coherently together.

Critical correction: this is a STRAIGHT-DOWN overhead sledgehammer smash that hits with ONE FLAT ROUND END CAP. At contact the BLUE CYLINDER'S LONG AXIS IS EXACTLY VERTICAL, its two caps are TOP and BOTTOM, and the BOTTOM CAP is level and faces STRAIGHT DOWN. The curved blue wall cannot be the striking surface. Absolutely no diagonal or sideways cylinder at impact.
The shaft enters the SIDE MIDPOINT of the cylinder, NEVER an end cap. At the downstroke/contact, the shaft points BACK INTO DEPTH from that side socket to both hands behind it, perpendicular to the vertical cylinder. It is naturally FORESHORTENED from the front view. Both hands grip close together at the actor's centerline. Allow the head/socket to partially occlude the shaft and hands; don't cheat by swinging it diagonally across the chest to display its full length. The correct physical hammer must stay rigid.

TOP LEFT: deepest over-and-behind-head windup; close hands behind the crown, elbows bent, the heavy hammer cocked behind upper back. Original face forward.
TOP RIGHT: hammer has come over the crown and is descending STRAIGHT DOWN IN FRONT OF THE BODY on its central vertical path; hands drive forward/down, vertical cylinder now around upper-chest height, both top/bottom caps level. The side-mounted shaft recedes toward the close hands.
BOTTOM LEFT: exact low impact pose. The same VERTICAL cylinder between and IN FRONT OF THE KNEES, BOTTOM CAP flat down at ground level in front of the boots, TOP CAP level above it. Both hands behind the cylinder at waist height grip its depth-foreshortened side-mounted handle. Deeply braced knees, shoulders forward, head/visor upright at viewer.
BOTTOM RIGHT: impact compression, same upright vertical cylinder and same bottom cap contacting exactly the same spot, knees compress a little farther. NO horizontal waist sweep.

Keep whole robot, hammer, fingers and fins inside generous transparent margins. Same armor/limb/core proportions throughout, fixed planted feet. No separate parts, no head stamping, no new face/jaw/crown, no impact art, glow clouds, trails, floor, labels or text. This is production sprite art, not a diagram.

Identity-preserving continuation of reference 1: FOUR complete Chronos robot+held hammer drawings in equal 640x640 cells, transparent 2x2 sheet. Same fixed frontal camera, exact body/head/core/limb unit and planted boot baseline as reference 1. Reference 2 locks his original small closed dark finned helmet and thin cyan visor: keep head upright facing straight forward, no redesign. Reference 3 locks the blue cylindrical T-hammer with side-midpoint socket, black segmented shaft and round end caps. All figure/weapon parts drawn together, sharp detailed16-bit sprite artwork.

These are the missing poses for the SAME overhead end-cap smash in reference 1. Maintain its correct STRAIGHT VERTICAL hammer cylinder on the downstroke, flat bottom cap facing down, handle perpendicular and receding in depth toward both hands. Never substitute a diagonal waist sweep or handle into a cap.

TOP LEFT — ready/recovered guard: upright robot with both hands close at lower chest, upright vertical blue cylinder low in front of his abdomen/thighs. Its handle extends back in depth from side-center socket to close hands, foreshortened, not a long diagonal bar.
TOP RIGHT — lifting into windup: hands above forehead beginning to draw the handle back behind the head, elbows bent beside the head; correct hammer is passing high over the crown. Preserve full fins/face.
BOTTOM LEFT — early FORWARD DOWNSTROKE after reference1 top-left behind-head pose: hands extend forward from above the crown, the same upright VERTICAL cylinder HIGH in front of the face/upper chest, below raised hands. Its flat bottom cap leads straight DOWN, shaft recedes behind its SIDE CENTER toward close hands. This must join reference1 top-right without a sideways drift.
BOTTOM RIGHT — PRE-CONTACT / REBOUND: vertical blue cylinder lower than reference1 top-right but higher than reference1 bottom-left contact. Bottom cap at lower-shin height, immediately in front of center between boots; knees bent, fists close behind side socket. Same straight down/up path.

No body translation or hop. Same canonical head and body dimensions, no per-cell fitting. Cylinder remains one rigid consistent hammer; head length and shaft do not grow. Whole head, boots and hammer within generous empty margins. No floor, effects, trails, labels, text, detached parts or separate props.

Use case identity-preserve. FOUR complete Chronos robot+held hammer sprites, transparent 2x2 sheet, four even640x640 cells, common planted boot baseline/body unit. Reference1 is the exact whole robot appearance and scale; reference2 is his unchanged original finned helmet and cyan visor; reference3 is his immutable blue cylindrical T-HAMMER. Crisp detailed16bit sprite pixels, fixed front camera. The original head looks straight at the viewer throughout. Whole body, arms, hands, shaft and mallet drawn together.

A powerful HORIZONTAL SIDE SWING from HIS RIGHT across toward SCREEN LEFT. It strikes with the LEFT ROUND END CAP OF THE CYLINDER. THE CYLINDER'S LONG AXIS MUST BE HORIZONTAL LEFT-TO-RIGHT IN EVERY ACTIVE/CONTACT POSE. Its two round flat end caps are LEFT and RIGHT, NEVER top and bottom during the active swing. The left flat cap faces screen-left and leads the blow; the curved blue barrel wall must not be the striking face. Do not copy the upright cylinder orientation of reference3 into the side impact.

RIGID T GEOMETRY: the long black segmented handle attaches to SIDE MIDPOINT of the horizontal cylinder, perpendicular in3D. During contact the handle points BACK INTO DEPTH toward his close two-handed grip, naturally foreshortened. The hands and shaft are BEHIND the hammer, not beyond an end cap. Show the side-center joint or perspective cues; never insert shaft into either end cap. Do not force the shaft/cylinder into a flat diagonal cross just to show both. The existing hammer is turned as a rigid object, no changing its design.

TOP LEFT: load the side strike to screen-right of his upper body, elbows bent, both hands close on shaft; blue cylinder already horizontal, ready to send its left end cap leftward. Head upright/front.
TOP RIGHT: arms drive across the front toward screen-left, horizontal hammerhead around lower chest level, LEFT cap leading. Torso/hips brace naturally, same limb/body unit, planted boots.
BOTTOM LEFT: FULL LEFT CONTACT, both arms reach left/forward, hammer cylinder horizontal at left flank just beyond his left forearm. Its left circular cap is the extreme leading surface and is perpendicular to the horizontal motion. Shaft recedes back to the close grips from SIDE CENTER, not a cap. Face stays forward.
BOTTOM RIGHT: follow-through just past the same LEFT contact, hammer cylinder still horizontal, left end cap still leading; elbows begin softening. No head turn, no pose teleport or weapon swap.

Generous margins for full arm reach and hammer; every pixel inside each cell. No effects, background, floor, labels, text, separate body parts or floating props. No diagonal cylinder at contact, no vertical barrel in a side strike.

Correct rigid geometry for FOUR full-body Chronos SIDE-SWING sprites. Transparent 2x2 grid, even640x640 cells, same body unit/pivot/boot baseline, generous margins. Ref1 locks the full robot; ref2 exact unchanged small dark helmet/thin cyan visor; ref3 original electric blue CYLINDRICAL T-HAMMER with two round black END CAPS and segmented long handle into SIDE MIDPOINT. Head upright faces viewer in every cell. Complete figure and weapon drawn together; crisp16bit metallic sprites.

THE WEAPON MUST FORM A LITERAL CLEAR T SHAPE ON SCREEN in all four poses:
  horizontal blue cylinder runs LEFT--RIGHT across the TOP;
  its black shaft projects STRAIGHT DOWN from the cylinder's exact SIDE-CENTER;
  both close-together hands grip that VERTICAL shaft BELOW the cylinder.
The handle NEVER enters the left/right circular endcap. The two caps are LEFT and RIGHT. Preserve visible T joint (top crossbar and downstroke stem). The round LEFT CAP points LEFT, ready to hit LEFT. This is the canonical hammer rotated to a horizontal head; not an axial club, not a vertical barrel on a horizontal shaft.

A leftward horizontal side blow at upper-chest/head height:
TOP LEFT: wind up at screen-RIGHT shoulder, arms bent. T-shaped hammer held upright to right, horizontal head above fists, vertical shaft down through both close hands.
TOP RIGHT: drive both hands across chest toward LEFT. Keep same upright T shape: horizontal blue head and DOWNWARD VERTICAL handle. Left cap leads left.
BOTTOM LEFT: full leftward contact. Both arms reach screen-LEFT, elbows nearly extended; fists still one above the other on the VERTICAL handle at lower-chest height. Horizontal blue cylinder ABOVE those fists near shoulder/head height. LEFT circular endcap is farthest left, flat face perpendicular to the LEFTWARD blow. The correct T joint is clearly visible ABOVE the hands.
BOTTOM RIGHT: slight leftward follow-through/recoil from the same contact, same T shape and endcap-leading direction.

Do not turn the robot head. No extra limbs, no separate pasted hammer, no new head/crown/jaw, no effects/text/floor. Keep COMPLETE extended hammer and every boot/fin inside each cell with AT LEAST 40 pixels clear padding at all edges; never clip the left cap. Keep hammer length/diameter/handle and body dimensions identical across all poses.
